subject.title: Background PTY exec runs can survive restart/session loss and become untracked orphan process trees

question: Should OpenClaw kill, reattach/re-register, or intentionally ignore PTY-backed background exec runs that survive a gateway restart without tracked session ownership?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the durable fix changes long-running task semantics and operator expectations, so automation should not choose the permanent policy alone.

options.title: Kill stale previous-epoch PTY runs
options.body: On startup, terminate persisted PTY exec runs from a prior gateway epoch that cannot be safely re-owned, with logging and tests for normal finalize cleanup.

options.title: Reattach previous runs
options.body: Persist enough metadata to validate and re-register surviving process trees after restart, accepting more complexity to preserve legitimate long-running work.

options.title: Land in-process cleanup only
options.body: Treat the open PR's session-drift reconciliation as a partial mitigation and leave cold-start orphan reaping for a later policy decision.

recommendation.title: Kill stale previous-epoch PTY runs
recommendation.body: On startup, terminate persisted PTY exec runs from a prior gateway epoch that cannot be safely re-owned, with logging and tests for normal finalize cleanup.
